# Single-Database Rewards Are Hackable: Counterfactual Execution for Trustworthy Text-to-SQL RL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#counterfactual-sql-rewards)

**Reading coverage:** Read Sections 1–5, references and Appendices A–E, including both figures and Tables 1–8. Checked the original PDF renderings of Figures 1 and 2. Artifact inspection covered public documentation and file inventories.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Pinned code and release documentation](https://github.com/RishiiGamer2201/counterfactual-sql-rewards/blob/d38373a4a7140bcca9890066c491e9205d9944f0/README.md) · [Pinned dataset card and licensing details](https://huggingface.co/datasets/counterfactual-sql/counterfactual-sql-data/blob/8bf2b42a1578534a2dbd630b5bb12479bc0f12df/README.md)

## Research question

Different SQL programs can produce the same rows on a particular database. An execution-based grader that credits both can reward an incorrect calculation.

## Method

The agent can inspect the original SQLite database. The grader runs its final SQL and the reference on additional hidden instances. One reward requires agreement everywhere. The main training reward requires agreement on the original and then pays in proportion to the hidden-instance matches. Generated references are cross-checked against a separate pandas calculation.

## Evaluation

The synthetic audit has 1,302 items from a retail schema. It scores fixed correct queries and deliberately flawed alternatives. The training comparison holds initialization and settings constant across reward arms for a 3.35B model and three seeds. Evaluation uses 331 items from seven held-out templates and a separate Spider transfer test.

## What the results support

With the same multiset comparator, the fraction of buggy variants paid in full falls from 29.5% on the original database to 16.8% with blind copy selection. Neither rejects any of the 2,847 designated correct queries. Across training seeds, verified in-domain sample accuracy is 8.4% with the multi-instance reward and 11.7% with single-instance training. The small average Spider gain changes sign across seeds.

## Limits and qualifications

All generated items use one retail schema and pass construction filters for deterministic, non-degenerate reference outputs. An incorrect reference is outside the study. Counterfactual tests still miss errors. The Spider transfer test was exploratory, and inference across three training seeds is imprecise.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful when assessing alternative SQL that agrees with a reference by coincidence. It evaluates reference agreement under changed data. It does not determine whether a user meant the reference calculation, or evaluate a policy for asking or abstaining.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Which comparison isolates the benefit of testing more databases? | Table 1 keeps the row comparator fixed and changes the databases graded. Among 1,814 buggy candidates, full payment falls from 29.5% to 16.8% with blind copy selection. The much lower 1.5% uses copies chosen against known errors. | Section 2, Table 1 and Appendix A | Use the blind result for the audit comparison. Selection informed by known mistakes gives an optimistic estimate for unseen errors. |
| Did a stricter audit produce a better trained agent? | The strict reward headlines the audit. The main training arm instead gates on the original result and averages hidden-copy matches. The reward signals differ on about 5–7% of training rollouts. At seed level the reported interval for the in-domain difference spans −13.7 to +7.3 percentage points, and for Spider it spans −3.2 to +6.4. | Sections 2–4, Figure 2, Appendix D Table 8 | The audit benefit and the learning result answer different questions. The sign reversal across seeds limits claims about transfer or training harm. |
| Does passing every test identify the right interpretation? | The held-out suite exposed 54 of 103 buggy variants that passed on the original instance. The paper also notes ties and ambiguous references when interpreting Spider suite failures. | Section 5, Appendix A and Appendix D Table 7 | A passing candidate has survived a finite reference-based check. A failing query on Spider can warrant inspection of the reference itself. |
